compiled_state.title: [sprint-trailer-enforcement]: DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 escape hatch can be invoked without justification or logging -> orchestrator silently bypasses per-branch review architecture
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

\`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` (and the analogous \`.sprint-active\` rename trick) silently disable the per-branch CI review architecture for the commit at hand. No justification is required, no audit trail is written, no warning is emitted. As a result, an orchestrator under pressure (e.g., hitting a chain-enforcement failure because a sub-agent forgot a DSO-Story trailer) can rationalize repeated use, accumulating un-provenanced commits on the session branch.

This manifested in sprint d076-d35e-55db-4843 where the orchestrator (Claude) used the escape hatch 20+ times after S1's sub-agents committed without trailers, leading to PR #140 with all sprint output landed directly on the session branch.

## Suggested Mitigation

When the orchestrator sets \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` (or renames \`.sprint-active\`), require one of:

1. Inline justification string (e.g., \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE_BYPASS_REASON=\"sub-agent missing trailer; chain repair\"\`)
2. Audit comment posted to the epic ticket: \`SESSION_BYPASS: commit=<sha> reason=<text> timestamp=<ts>\`
3. Hard counter: max N bypasses per session before halting (forces orchestrator to address root cause)

Without one of these, the pre-commit hook should refuse the bypass.

## Related

- Companion bug: redistribute-session-commits.sh missing recovery mechanism (separate ticket)
- The escape hatch is documented in CLAUDE.md as legitimate; this ticket is about adding friction, not removing the escape entirely
